Now I have sufficient evidence to construct my forecast. Let me compile the findings:

- **S&P Global Flash Manufacturing PMI (May 2026)**: rose to 55.3, 48-month high (vs 54.5 in April); output sub-index 56.2 (49-month high)
- **ISM April 2026**: PMI 52.7; New Orders 54.1, Production 53.4, Supplier Deliveries 60.6, Employment 46.4
- **Richmond Fed May 2026**: composite +13 (from +3 in April); new orders +17
- **Philadelphia Fed May 2026**: general activity fell to -0.4 (from ~27.5), lowest of 2026
- **Dallas Fed May 2026**: production slowed to 9.4 (from 19.0), general business activity barely positive at 0.4
- **Kansas City Fed May 2026**: composite +8 (from 10), activity continued to increase

The S&P Global reading at 55.3 is significantly above ISM's April print of 52.7 (the gap in April was 54.5 - 52.7 = 1.8 pts). Applying a similar gap suggests ISM May ≈ 53.5. Richmond improved sharply; Kansas City continued expanding. The Philly Fed collapse (-0.4 from ~27.5) is a strong offset but historically very volatile (avg absolute monthly change 8.2 pts). Dallas slowed but remained expansionary.
